meta.title: Open BIM Collaborator — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open BIM Collaborator: check the models of every discipline together. Test them against IDS and the NL-BIM Basis ILS, find clashes, compare versions and record agreements as BCF issues. Part of Open BIM Suite.

header.label: Coming soon · BIM coordination
header.title: Open BIM Collaborator
header.desc: Put the models of every discipline side by side, test them against IDS and the NL-BIM Basis ILS, find clashes, compare versions and record agreements as BCF issues. All on your own computer, as part of Open BIM Suite.

notice.text: Coming soon: the Collaborator is already part of the desktop version of Open BIM Suite, but it cannot be downloaded on its own yet and does not work in the web version yet. Do not use it for real project work yet. Report what you run into on GitHub.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From separate models to agreements
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic. This is what the desktop version can do now.

check.title: Test the model against the requirements
check.desc: Load an IDS file or pick the bundled NL-BIM Basis ILS or RVB BIM Norm. Per rule you see what failed, what is a warning, what cannot be checked and what passed, with a score from A to E. One click on a finding takes you to the element.

clash.title: Find where disciplines collide
clash.desc: Find intersections, too little clearance or a blocked line of sight between structure, services and architecture. The Collaborator works on the real geometry, groups the clashes and shows what is new and what is resolved since the last run.

isolate.title: Look at every clash on its own
isolate.desc: Isolate a clash so only the elements involved remain, put a section box around it and accept or reject it with one key. Turn a clash, a group or everything at once into an issue.

rvb.title: Save your check and run it again
rvb.desc: A rule set keeps your IDS files, clash tests, tolerances, selection sets and earlier decisions in one file. That way you check every new version of the model the same way. Four rule sets come built in.

federate.title: Federate models
federate.desc: Open the models of the architect, structural engineer and services engineer together in one project, each with its own visibility switch.

formats.title: Any format alongside
formats.desc: IFC, IFCX, STEP, DWG, DXF, Revit, SketchUp, glTF and point clouds: everything Open BIM Suite opens. The checks work on IFC.

ids.title: IDS checking
ids.desc: Test a model against any IDS 1.0 file. What the check cannot judge is marked "not checkable", never "passed".

ils.title: NL-BIM Basis ILS
ils.desc: File name, storey names and heights, NL-SfB, material, load-bearing, external, fire rating and proxies, with your own pattern for storey names.

rvb.title: RVB BIM Norm 1.1
rvb.desc: The requirements of the Dutch Central Government Real Estate Agency as a bundled IDS file.

modelchecks.title: Built-in model checks
modelchecks.desc: Duplicate or crossing elements, missing units, circular references, proxies, elements without material or type, and elements outside a storey.

rooms.title: Rooms, doors and escape routes
rooms.desc: Room numbers, clear height, door sizes, thresholds, ramps, turning circles, fire doors and the walking distance to an exit. You set the limits yourself.

score.title: Score from A to E
score.desc: Every run gives a quality score from 0 to 100, so you see whether the model improves.

clashtests.title: Three kinds of clash test
clashtests.desc: Intersection (2 mm by default), clearance (50 mm by default) and line of sight, for instance whether escape route signs are visible.

matrix.title: Discipline matrix
matrix.desc: Per test, choose side A and B by model, layer or IFC class, only between models, per storey, and with a tolerance per type pair.

classify.title: Classified and grouped
classify.desc: Touching, partial, through or duplicate element. Group per element or per location, and see what is new and what is resolved.

review.title: Accept or reject
review.desc: Go through the clashes with keyboard shortcuts, isolate them and put a section box around them. Your decisions are kept.

newissue.title: Issue from the view
newissue.desc: An issue keeps the camera, the selection, hidden elements, the section, measurements, notes and an image. One click takes you back to that viewpoint.

fields.title: Everything an issue needs
fields.desc: Title, description, status, priority, type, assignee, due date, labels and comments. Search the list and hide closed issues.

bcf.title: BCF in and out
bcf.desc: Open BCF 2.0, 2.1 and 3.0. Save as BCF 2.1 or 3.0, so other BIM software can read the issues.

fromfindings.title: Issues from findings
fromfindings.desc: Create an issue per failed rule or per clash in one click, with the wrong elements already selected.

compare.title: Compare versions
compare.desc: Put two versions side by side and see what was added, removed or changed, in properties and in position or size down to a millimetre.

colours.title: Colour by property
colours.desc: Colour the model by model, layer, class, type or any property, with a legend. Select a value or save it as a set.

sets.title: Selection sets
sets.desc: Save a selection and use it to select, isolate or hide, also in clash tests.

takeoff.title: Quantities
takeoff.desc: Filter by class or property, group by two properties and get count, length, area and volume in a table.

rulesets.title: Rule sets
rulesets.desc: Keep IDS files, clash tests, tolerances, sets, quantity schedules, room rules and decisions in one file. Four rule sets come built in.

exports.title: Reports
exports.desc: Export the results as PDF with images, Excel, HTML, CSV or JSON, and the issues as an HTML or PDF report.

mcp.title: Operable by AI
mcp.desc: Through the built-in MCP server an AI assistant can create issues, run checks and clash tests, compare and export. Everything runs locally.

local.title: On your own computer
local.desc: The models and the checks stay on your own computer. Nothing is sent to a server.

whatsnew.label: Already in the desktop version
whatsnew.title: Further along than it looks: almost everything already works
whatsnew.desc: The Collaborator is the third module of Open BIM Suite, next to the Viewer and the Modeller. On the desktop the features below already work. Not ready yet: a separate installer, the web version, and sharing through a server or the SuperCloud.

checks.title: IDS and room checks
checks.desc: IDS 1.0, the NL-BIM Basis ILS, the RVB BIM Norm and checks on rooms, doors and escape routes work in the desktop version.

clashes.title: Clashes on the real geometry
clashes.desc: Intersection, clearance and line of sight, with a discipline matrix, groups and a decision per clash.

bcf.title: BCF 3.0
bcf.desc: Open issues in BCF 2.0, 2.1 and 3.0 and save them as 2.1 or 3.0.

compare.title: Compare, colours and quantities
compare.desc: Compare versions by GlobalId, colour the model by property and see quantities in a table.

status.q: Can I use Open BIM Collaborator already?
status.a: Not on its own yet. The features are in the desktop version of Open BIM Suite, which you switch to the Collaborator with the switch at the top right. A separate installer and the web version will follow. Do not use it for real project work yet.

suite.q: How does it relate to Open BIM Suite?
suite.a: Open BIM Suite is one program with three modules: the Viewer, the Modeller and the Collaborator. They share the same project, the same models and the same selection. The Collaborator will also come as a separate app.

cost.a: Nothing. The source code is free to use under the LGPL-3.0 licence.

ids.a: The Information Delivery Specification is an open buildingSMART standard to record information requirements in a file that software can read. Such a file says, for example, that every wall must have an NL-SfB code and a fire rating.

compliance.q: Does my model meet the standard if everything passes?
compliance.a: Not necessarily. The bundled files for the NL-BIM Basis ILS and the RVB BIM Norm are our own rendering of those standards. Requirements that IDS cannot capture you judge separately. Check an approved escape route on the drawing as well: the check works with straight lines.

data.a: On your own computer. The Collaborator reads, checks and compares everything locally and sends nothing to a server.

share.q: Can I share issues with my team?
share.a: Through a BCF file, which any package with BCF support can open. Sharing through a shared folder, a BCF server or the OpenAEC SuperCloud is planned.

related.q: How does it differ from BIM Validator and BCF Manager Studio?
related.a: The Collaborator brings checking, clashes and issues together in one program and so replaces BIM Validator on the homepage. BCF Manager Studio remains a separate tool to manage BCF issues.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: Part of Open BIM Suite: the same core as the Viewer and the Modeller.

rust.title: Rust
rust.desc: The whole app, from reading the models to the checks and the clashes, in one fast program.

gpu.title: iced and wgpu
gpu.desc: The interface and the 3D view on the graphics card, on Windows, macOS and Linux.

validator.title: bim-validator-core
validator.desc: The validation core with the model checks, the ILS profile and the room checks.

standards.title: IFC, IDS and BCF
standards.desc: The open buildingSMART standards for the model, the requirements and the issues.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.desc: A local MCP server with which an AI assistant can operate the Collaborator.

ifcx.title: IFCX
ifcx.desc: Projects and models can be saved as IFCX, the open format of the OpenAEC ecosystem.
